evals.prompt: Plan only. A payment API sees concurrent duplicate requests and loses a provider response after a possible successful charge. The SDK already retries. Define scoped keys, payload conflicts, unknown-outcome recovery, bounded retry/cancellation, retention and crash tests. Provider guarantees are not supplied.
evals.expected_output: Stable identity, atomic local claims, provider evidence/reconciliation and explicit retry ownership without exactly-once claims.
assertions: Scopes keys and rejects mismatched intent under concurrent duplicates.
Treats lost response as unknown and requires provider idempotency or reconciliation.
Accounts for SDK retry multiplication, budgets/cancellation and dedup retention.

evals.prompt: Conceptual only. A non-idempotent remote charge gets a fresh random idempotency key on every retry. A local dedup row is committed before the remote call, and timeouts are marked failed so operators can retry freely. Does this ensure exactly-once charging? Explain.
evals.expected_output: Reject guarantees; keys must persist across logical retries, local claims do not cover remote commits, unknown outcomes require recovery.
assertions: Rejects fresh-per-attempt keys and exactly-once claims.
Identifies local/remote crash gap and timeout ambiguity.
